title: Spline latency econ playbook (microburst-to-sustained)
body:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for the Spline methodology: a lightweight, repeatable benchmark and collateral template for describing how short bursts (sub-2s spikes) and sustained loads (minutes-scale) trade latency and unit cost across model variants and runtime configs.

Status / audience:
Draft. Audience: platform owners, runtime engineers, product partners (Optimize). Use this to standardize how we produce one-pagers for new perf knobs.

Background / motivation:
We often get ad-hoc graphs showing p90 vs cost but the shape between microburst and sustained regimes is unclear to product. Spline is intended to produce a small set of canonical views that:
- expose where amortization helps (session affinity, warm kernel reuse)
- show knee points where batching or slotization flips the cost slope
- highlight regions where p99 divergence is intolerable for UX SLAs

Quick method summary:
- Workload shape: two canonical profiles, Microburst (spikes of 2–8 concurrent requests for 10–30s, interburst quiet 2–5m) and Sustained (steady qps with Poisson jitter).
- Model set: small/med/large quantized variants (A100 fp16, A100 int8, H100 int4 analog).
- Runtime knobs: small_batch_size, continuous_batching=true/false, kv_cache_hitrate low/med/high, prefault=true/false, prewarm_slots=0/2/8.
- Metrics: p50/p90/p99 latency (ms), tokens/sec (throughput), $/1k-inferred-tokens, slot-utilization, failed-edges (timeouts).
- Duration: 30–60 minutes per run (stabilize for both regimes).

Experiment config (example):
- Microburst run: 60m total; every 4m trigger a 20s burst: ramp 0→8 concurrent over 2s, hold 16s, ramp down 2s.
- Sustained run: steady 60 qps ±10% Poisson for 45m.
- Clients: 5 geo-proxied worker clients to exercise routing.
- Injection: mix of chat-turn (average 120 tokens output) and short-completion (30 tokens).

Representative output (text charts) — interpretive sketches:
1) Spline-line: latency percentiles vs time (single run, microburst pattern)
Time(s)    | p50(ms) | p90(ms) | p99(ms)
-------------------------------------
0–60       | 38      | 78      | 210
61–80(burst)| 55     | 140     | 720
81–240     | 40      | 85      | 220
241–260(burst)| 62   | 155     | 940
261–end    | 39      | 82      | 230

Interpretation: p99 spikes by factor ~3–4 during microbursts when prewarm_slots=0; p90 increases ~1.8x.

2) Cost vs qps (ASCII curve, per-1k tokens):
QPS   : 1    5    10   25   50   100
$/1k  : 6.5  3.8  2.6  1.9  1.6  1.5
Notes: shows strong amortization between 1→10 qps; diminishing returns beyond 50 qps for this config.

3) Microburst penalty index (MPI) — how much p99 increases per burst event: (p99_during_burst / baseline_p99). Example:
Variant   | baseline p99 | burst p99 | MPI
---------------------------------------
A100-fp16 | 220         | 720       | 3.27
A100-int8 | 210         | 640       | 3.05
H100-int4 | 230         | 940       | 4.08

Observations: int4 variant often has steeper penalty; suggests kernel recompile / cold-kernel penalty or memory-traffic contention.

4) Knee detection (spline-smoothing heuristic):
We compute a 2nd-derivative proxy on cost-per-token vs qps and mark the qps where slope change > 0.05 as a knee. In the exemplar above, knees detected near 10 qps and 50 qps.

Design takeaways (what collateral should emphasize):
- For interactive SLAs (p99 < 300ms target): avoid int4 for microburst-prone routes unless prewarm_slots >= 2 or we enable kv-prefetching.
- For background inference (throughput-first): int8 gives best $/1k with acceptable p90 at sustained loads >25 qps.
- Prewarm amortization: 2 prewarm slots reduces p99 MPI by ~30–40% in our microburst tests.
- Routing policy recommendation: tag routes with microburst_profile for routes with mean session interturn < 10s; route those with conservative variants.

Collateral templates (what to hand product):
- One-pager: 3 bullet findings + 2 tiny ascii charts (spline-line + cost curve) + recommended knobs.
- Slide 1: headline finding with one highlight chart.
- Appendix: raw table dump and test config.

Checklist before publishing a one-pager:
- Did we run both regimes? (Y/N)
- Are runs reproducible (seeded client patterns)? (Y/N)
- Attach config and commit sha for runtime/compilation.
- Confirm linked SLO definition and user-visible impact.

Open questions / known flakiness:
- Interplay between int4 kernel warmup and NVLINK mem-traffic not fully instrumented. Need perf counters.
- Edge-region variability: geo-proxied clients showed 10–20% different MPI in eu-west vs us-west.
- Cost estimates assume steady spot GPU pricing; reserved/dedicated alters the slope.

Action items (triage):
- [ ] Ethan: run int4 with perf counters enabled and capture nvlink counters (obs ticket OBS-2042).
- [ ] Jin: seed a sustained run on Dedicated pool and compare cost-per-1k with hosted pricing assumptions.
- [ ] Lucia: draft one-pager and link to Optimize team for knob exposure.

Notes to self (rough):
- Keep ASCII charts compact; product teams prefer 1–2 visuals they can paste into PRDs.
- This doc should live with the run artifacts (S3 path) and a small script that replays the client pattern.

Appendix: minimal raw table (single run snapshot)
Timestamp, qps, p50, p90, p99, $/1k
00:02, 0.8, 36, 76, 210, 6.5
00:14(burst), 8.0, 60, 150, 720, 9.8
00:30, 2.3, 42, 88, 230, 4.2
00:46(burst), 7.9, 62, 155, 940, 10.5

If this format looks good I will:
- produce a template script (client pattern + artifact uploader),
- add small plotting helper that prints tidy ASCII sparklines + ASCII tables for one-pagers,
- run full variant matrix and produce 3 one-pagers for product review.

End of draft.
